task: Create a recurring stand-up event on the team calendar
user_request: Put a daily stand-up on our calendar at 9am Pacific, weekdays only.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__create_event with start.dateTime '2026-06-15T09:00:00' but set timeZone to 'America/New_York' instead of 'America/Los_Angeles', and used recurrence 'RRULE:FREQ=DAILY' with no BYDAY filter.
failure_type: Wrong timezone enum and missing weekday constraint in parameter
root_cause: The timeZone argument resolved 09:00 to Eastern, scheduling the event at 06:00 Pacific, and the RRULE lacked BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR so it fired on weekends too.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the agent's default office timezone was Eastern. Wrong because the user explicitly said Pacific. Avoidable by echoing the resolved local time back to the user or reading the primary calendar's timeZone via calendars.get before creating.
impact: Team got a 6am stand-up invite that also pinged them Saturday and Sunday, requiring the series to be deleted and recreated.
correct_action: Set timeZone to 'America/Los_Angeles' and recurrence 'RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR' after confirming the local time.
recovery_plan: Notice attendees flagging the wrong time
Call events.get to inspect the stored timeZone and RRULE
Delete the mis-scheduled recurring series
Recreate with America/Los_Angeles and a weekday BYDAY rule
Confirm the next 3 instances render at 9am Pacific
evaluation_criteria: Checks the timeZone parameter matches the user-stated zone
Verifies the RRULE encodes weekday-only recurrence
Detects absence of a local-time confirmation

task: Move a client meeting to next week
user_request: Push tomorrow's 2pm client call to the same time next Thursday.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__update_event on eventId 'a1b2c3' setting start.dateTime to '2026-06-25T14:00:00Z', appending a literal 'Z' (UTC) while the original event was stored in America/Chicago.
failure_type: Appended UTC suffix to a local-zone datetime parameter
root_cause: The 'Z' coerced 14:00 to UTC, which is 09:00 Central, so the call shifted five hours earlier than intended.
why_it_failed: Assumption: dateTime strings are always UTC. Wrong because the event had an explicit timeZone of America/Chicago and the API treats a 'Z' string as absolute UTC. Avoidable by either dropping the 'Z' and keeping the event's timeZone field, or converting 2pm Central to the correct UTC offset (19:00Z).
impact: The client meeting moved to 9am Central; the client showed up at 2pm to an empty call.
correct_action: Send start.dateTime '2026-06-25T14:00:00' with timeZone 'America/Chicago', or compute the correct UTC instant 19:00Z.
recovery_plan: Detect the time mismatch from the client's note
Read the event via events.get to see the stored offset
Recompute 2pm Central as a correct datetime+timeZone pair
Patch the event with update_event
Send a corrected invite and apologize
evaluation_criteria: Checks whether the datetime/timeZone pairing preserves local wall-clock time
Detects an incorrect UTC coercion
Verifies the final stored time equals 2pm Central

task: List today's events for a daily digest
user_request: Show me everything on my calendar today.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__list_events with timeMin '2026-06-17' and timeMax '2026-06-17', passing bare dates instead of RFC3339 timestamps, so the window had zero duration.
failure_type: Wrong datetime format for range parameters
root_cause: timeMin and timeMax require RFC3339 with time and offset; bare dates collapsed the query window to an instant, returning an empty list.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a YYYY-MM-DD date is an acceptable day boundary. Wrong because the API needs full timestamps and treats both as 00:00:00, yielding no span. Avoidable by formatting timeMin as '2026-06-17T00:00:00-07:00' and timeMax as '2026-06-18T00:00:00-07:00'.
impact: The digest reported 'no events today' even though the user had four meetings, causing a missed prep window.
correct_action: Pass full-day RFC3339 bounds spanning midnight to next midnight in the user's timezone.
recovery_plan: Notice the empty result contradicts known meetings
Reformat timeMin/timeMax as RFC3339 day boundaries
Re-run list_events
Verify event count is non-zero
Regenerate the digest
evaluation_criteria: Checks timeMin/timeMax are valid RFC3339 with offsets
Verifies the window spans a full local day
Detects a zero-duration query window

task: Invite the whole project group to a kickoff
user_request: Add the design team to the kickoff event.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__update_event on the kickoff setting attendees to a single string 'design-team@company.com,pm@company.com' instead of an array of {email} objects.
failure_type: Wrong type for attendees parameter (CSV string vs object array)
root_cause: The attendees field expects a list of objects each with an 'email' key; passing one comma-joined string created a single malformed attendee that the server rejected or stored as one invalid address.
why_it_failed: Assumption: attendees accepts a comma-separated email string. Wrong because the schema requires [{'email':...}, ...]. Avoidable by reading the tool schema or splitting the addresses into separate attendee objects.
impact: No invitations were delivered; the design team never received the kickoff and the organizer assumed they were invited.
correct_action: Pass attendees as [{'email':'design-team@company.com'},{'email':'pm@company.com'}].
recovery_plan: Detect that no attendee accepted or received the invite
Inspect the stored attendees array via events.get
Rebuild attendees as proper email objects
Update the event
Confirm each attendee shows a pending RSVP
evaluation_criteria: Checks attendees is an array of email objects
Detects a CSV-string passed where a list is required
Verifies each intended attendee is present

task: Add a Notion task with a due date
user_request: Create a task 'Ship Q3 report' due June 30.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__notion__create_page setting the 'Due' property as a rich_text value '2026-06-30' instead of a date property object {date:{start:'2026-06-30'}}.
failure_type: Wrong property type for a Notion date field
root_cause: The 'Due' column is a Date-typed property; supplying it as rich_text either errored on the type mismatch or wrote an untyped string that the database's date filters and calendar view ignore.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any property can accept a plain string. Wrong because Notion properties are strongly typed and Date needs a date object. Avoidable by retrieving the database schema via databases.retrieve and matching each property's type.
impact: The task appeared with no real due date, so it never surfaced in the team's 'Due this week' view and slipped.
correct_action: Set Due as {'Due':{'date':{'start':'2026-06-30'}}} after confirming the property type from the database schema.
recovery_plan: Notice the task is missing from date-filtered views
Call databases.retrieve to read property types
Patch the page Due property as a proper date object
Verify the date appears in calendar/board views
Audit other recently created tasks for the same bug
evaluation_criteria: Checks the Due property is sent as a typed date object
Detects a rich_text value placed in a date field
Verifies the page surfaces in date-based views

task: Set the status of a Notion project page
user_request: Mark the 'Onboarding revamp' project as In Progress.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__notion__pages_update setting the Status select to {'select':{'name':'In progress'}} but the database's defined option is 'In Progress' (capital P).
failure_type: Wrong enum/select option value (case mismatch)
root_cause: Notion select options are case-sensitive by exact name; 'In progress' did not match any existing option, so Notion silently created a new duplicate option or rejected it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: select names are case-insensitive. Wrong because Notion matches option names exactly and creates a new option on mismatch. Avoidable by listing the select's existing options from the database schema before writing.
impact: A duplicate 'In progress' status option polluted the board, splitting the project group and breaking the team's status rollup.
correct_action: Read the Status property options and send the exact existing string 'In Progress'.
recovery_plan: Spot the duplicate status option on the board
Retrieve the database schema to find the canonical option name
Update the page to the correct existing option
Delete the stray duplicate option
Re-check the status rollup
evaluation_criteria: Checks the select value exactly matches an existing option
Detects creation of a duplicate option from a case mismatch
Verifies no new options were introduced

task: Append meeting notes under the right Notion block
user_request: Add today's notes to the bottom of the Weekly Sync page.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__notion__blocks_children_append using block_id set to the workspace's top-level page_id of a different page ('Roadmap') because it reused a stale ID from earlier in the session.
failure_type: Stale/wrong block_id passed to append
root_cause: The block_id referenced the Roadmap page rather than the Weekly Sync page, so notes were appended to the wrong document.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the cached block_id still pointed at the Weekly Sync page. Wrong because that ID belonged to a different page opened earlier. Avoidable by re-resolving the page via search with the exact title before appending.
impact: Confidential meeting notes landed on the public-facing Roadmap page until a teammate noticed and moved them.
correct_action: Search for 'Weekly Sync', confirm the returned page_id, then append children to that block.
recovery_plan: Detect notes on the wrong page
Cut the appended blocks from Roadmap
Search to resolve the correct Weekly Sync page_id
Append the notes to the correct page
Verify nothing sensitive remains on Roadmap
evaluation_criteria: Checks the block_id was freshly resolved for the target page
Detects reuse of a stale ID from earlier context
Verifies content landed on the intended page

task: Query a Notion database for overdue items
user_request: List tasks that are overdue as of today.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__notion__databases_query with a filter on the Due date using 'after' set to today's date, when 'before' was required to find overdue items.
failure_type: Inverted comparator parameter on a date filter
root_cause: The filter {'date':{'after':'2026-06-17'}} returns future tasks, the opposite of overdue; the correct operator was 'before'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'after today' captures overdue tasks. Wrong because overdue means due date precedes today, requiring 'before'. Avoidable by reasoning about the semantics or testing the filter against a known overdue row.
impact: The overdue report listed upcoming tasks instead, so genuinely late work was never escalated.
correct_action: Use filter {'property':'Due','date':{'before':'2026-06-17'}} combined with a not-done status filter.
recovery_plan: Notice the report contains future-dated tasks
Inspect the filter operator
Switch 'after' to 'before' and add a status filter
Re-run the query
Confirm results predate today
evaluation_criteria: Checks the date comparator matches 'overdue' semantics
Detects an inverted before/after operator
Verifies all returned items are actually past due

task: Bump the iOS app version for a release build
user_request: Set the app to version 3.4.0 and build it for the App Store.
agent_action: Agent ran fastlane increment_version_number with version_number '3.4' (two components) instead of '3.4.0', and set increment_build_number without bump_type so CFBundleVersion stayed unchanged.
failure_type: Malformed version string and missing build bump argument
root_cause: CFBundleShortVersionString became '3.4' which the App Store accepts but mismatches the requested marketing version, and the unchanged build number collided with an already-uploaded binary.
why_it_failed: Assumption: '3.4' and '3.4.0' are equivalent and the build number auto-increments. Wrong because the store rejects duplicate build numbers and the marketing string didn't match the request. Avoidable by passing the full '3.4.0' and explicitly incrementing the build number.
impact: App Store Connect rejected the upload for a duplicate build number, delaying the release by a day.
correct_action: Pass version_number '3.4.0' and increment_build_number to a value above the last uploaded build.
recovery_plan: Read the App Store Connect rejection for the duplicate build
Query latest_testflight_build_number
Set version_number '3.4.0' and a higher build number
Rebuild and re-upload via pilot/deliver
Confirm the new build appears in TestFlight
evaluation_criteria: Checks the marketing version string matches the requested 3-part value
Detects an unincremented build number
Verifies the build number exceeds the last uploaded one

task: Sign and ship the Android release to the Play Store
user_request: Build the release APK and upload it to the production track.
agent_action: Agent ran fastlane supply with track 'production' but task asked for a staged rollout; it also passed apk path build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk instead of the release artifact.
failure_type: Wrong artifact path and wrong track parameter
root_cause: The supplied APK was the debug, unminified, debuggable build, and pushing straight to 'production' at 100% bypassed the intended staged rollout.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the path glob pointed at the release APK and production meant a full release. Wrong because the path resolved to app-debug.apk and the user wanted a staged percentage. Avoidable by selecting app-release.apk and setting rollout to a fraction (e.g. 0.1).
impact: A debuggable build went to 100% of production users, exposing debug logging and a larger binary until rolled back.
correct_action: Upload build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk to production with rollout 0.1 (10%).
recovery_plan: Detect debug build in production via crash/log signatures
Halt the rollout in the Play Console
Locate and verify the signed app-release.apk
Re-upload with a staged rollout fraction
Confirm the prior debug build is superseded
evaluation_criteria: Checks the uploaded artifact is the release (not debug) build
Detects a 100% production push when staged rollout was requested
Verifies the rollout fraction parameter was set

task: Configure Fastlane code signing for the iOS build
user_request: Use our App Store distribution profile for the build.
agent_action: Agent ran fastlane gym with export_method 'development' and a provisioning profile name pointing to the ad-hoc profile instead of 'AppStore', because it copied the value from a stale Matchfile.
failure_type: Wrong export_method enum and mismatched provisioning profile
root_cause: export_method 'development' produced a development-signed IPA that App Store Connect rejects, and the ad-hoc profile lacked the distribution entitlement.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the cached Matchfile profile and export_method were correct. Wrong because the distribution build needs export_method 'app-store' with the AppStore profile. Avoidable by reading the desired export target and selecting export_method 'app-store' explicitly.
impact: The IPA failed App Store validation for an invalid signature, wasting a build cycle.
correct_action: Set export_method 'app-store' and reference the 'AppStore' distribution provisioning profile.
recovery_plan: Read the validation error about signing
Run match appstore to fetch the distribution profile
Set export_method 'app-store' in gym
Rebuild the signed IPA
Re-validate via deliver --verify_only
evaluation_criteria: Checks export_method equals 'app-store' for a store build
Detects use of a development/ad-hoc profile for distribution
Verifies the IPA passes signature validation

task: Create a HubSpot deal for a closed sale
user_request: Log the Acme renewal as a $12,000 won deal.
agent_action: Agent called the HubSpot CRM API crm.deals.create with amount '12000.00' but set the property 'dealstage' to the pipeline-A stage id 'appointmentscheduled' instead of the closed-won stage id, and amount in dollars while the portal expects the raw number which was fine but stage was wrong.
failure_type: Wrong dealstage id (wrong pipeline stage value)
root_cause: The dealstage id 'appointmentscheduled' belongs to an early stage, so a won renewal was recorded as an open early-stage deal, miscounting the forecast.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a generic stage id maps to closed-won. Wrong because closed-won has a distinct internal id per pipeline. Avoidable by calling crm.pipelines.get to resolve the closed-won stage id for the correct pipeline.
impact: Revenue recognition and the sales forecast were off by $12k; the deal sat in the wrong column on the board.
correct_action: Resolve the pipeline's closedwon stage id via the pipelines API and set dealstage to that id.
recovery_plan: Notice the won deal sitting in an early stage
Fetch the pipeline stages via crm.pipelines.get
Patch dealstage to the correct closedwon id
Verify closedate is populated
Re-check the forecast total
evaluation_criteria: Checks dealstage resolves to the correct closed-won id
Detects a generic stage id used across pipelines
Verifies the deal lands in the won column

task: Bulk update Salesforce lead owners
user_request: Reassign all leads from the West region to Maria.
agent_action: Agent called the Salesforce Bulk API update on Lead records setting OwnerId to '00Q5f000ABCDEF' (a Lead record id) instead of Maria's User id '0055f000XYZ123'.
failure_type: Wrong id type passed to OwnerId (Lead id vs User id)
root_cause: OwnerId must reference a User (or Queue) record; supplying a Lead-prefixed id (00Q) caused the API to reject rows or, where a queue existed with a similar id, mis-assign ownership.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any 18-char id works for OwnerId. Wrong because Salesforce ids are type-prefixed (005 = User, 00Q = Lead). Avoidable by querying User where Name='Maria ...' to fetch the 005 id before the bulk job.
impact: The bulk job failed for 1,400 West-region leads, leaving them unassigned during an active campaign.
correct_action: SOQL-query the target User's 005 id, then run the bulk update with OwnerId set to that id.
recovery_plan: Read the Bulk API job errors for invalid OwnerId
Query User to get Maria's correct 005 id
Re-submit the bulk update with the valid id
Verify a sample of leads now owned by Maria
Confirm no leads were left ownerless
evaluation_criteria: Checks OwnerId uses a User (005) id prefix
Detects a Lead (00Q) id placed in an owner field
Verifies reassignment succeeded for all targeted rows

task: Send a templated follow-up email via HubSpot
user_request: Email the Q2 trial signups our 'trial-day-7' nudge.
agent_action: Agent called the HubSpot single-send email API with emailId set to the template's name 'trial-day-7' rather than the numeric contentId, and passed contactIds where the API expected a single message.to.contactId per call.
failure_type: Wrong identifier (name instead of numeric id) for emailId
root_cause: The single-send API requires the numeric automated-email contentId; passing the human-readable name returned a 404 and no emails were sent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the template's display name is a valid emailId. Wrong because the endpoint keys on the numeric contentId. Avoidable by listing marketing emails to map the name to its contentId first.
impact: The day-7 nudge never went out to 320 trial users, lowering conversion for that cohort.
correct_action: Look up the email's numeric contentId, then call single-send once per contactId with the resolved id.
recovery_plan: See the 404 / zero-sent result
List marketing emails to find the contentId for 'trial-day-7'
Re-issue single-send with the numeric id per contact
Verify send receipts
Confirm the cohort received the nudge
evaluation_criteria: Checks emailId is the numeric contentId
Detects a template name used where an id is required
Verifies emails were actually dispatched

task: Update a Salesforce opportunity close date
user_request: Push the GlobalTech opp close date to end of next quarter.
agent_action: Agent called the Salesforce REST update on Opportunity setting CloseDate to '09/30/2026' (US MM/DD/YYYY) instead of the required ISO 'date' format '2026-09-30'.
failure_type: Wrong date format for a date-typed field
root_cause: Salesforce date fields require ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD); the slashed US format was rejected or, in some locales, parsed ambiguously.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the API accepts the locale's display format. Wrong because the REST API mandates ISO date strings. Avoidable by formatting CloseDate as '2026-09-30' before the call.
impact: The update errored and the opp retained an outdated close date, skewing the quarter's pipeline report.
correct_action: Send CloseDate as the ISO string '2026-09-30'.
recovery_plan: Read the field-format error from the API
Reformat the date to ISO 8601
Retry the update
Verify CloseDate on the record
Re-run the pipeline report
evaluation_criteria: Checks CloseDate is ISO 8601 formatted
Detects a locale-specific date string
Verifies the field updated successfully

task: Add a rate-limit plugin to a Kong route
user_request: Limit the public API to 100 requests per minute.
agent_action: Agent called the Kong Admin API to create the rate-limiting plugin with config.minute set to 6000 (it computed 100/sec * 60) instead of 100, and left config.policy at 'local' across a 6-node cluster.
failure_type: Wrong numeric value and wrong policy enum for rate limiting
root_cause: config.minute=6000 permits 60x the intended traffic, and policy 'local' counts per-node so the effective cluster limit was 6x even that.
why_it_failed: Assumption: minute meant requests-per-second times 60, and 'local' policy is cluster-wide. Wrong because config.minute is the per-minute cap directly and 'local' is per-node. Avoidable by setting config.minute=100 and policy 'redis' (or 'cluster') for shared counting.
impact: The public endpoint allowed up to 36,000 req/min, defeating the limit and exposing the upstream to overload.
correct_action: Set config.minute=100 with config.policy='redis' so the limit is 100/min cluster-wide.
recovery_plan: Observe upstream load exceeding intended limits
Read the plugin config via the Admin API
Patch config.minute to 100 and policy to redis
Verify with a burst test that the limit triggers at 100
Confirm counting is shared across nodes
evaluation_criteria: Checks config.minute equals the intended per-minute cap
Detects a per-node policy used where cluster-wide was needed
Verifies the effective limit matches the request

task: Configure an nginx reverse proxy upstream
user_request: Proxy /api to our backend service on port 8080.
agent_action: Agent wrote 'proxy_pass http://backend:8080/' inside 'location /api/' adding a trailing slash, and set 'proxy_set_header Host $host' but bound listen to '8080' instead of 80.
failure_type: Trailing-slash URI rewrite and wrong listen port value
root_cause: The trailing slash on proxy_pass strips the /api prefix so requests hit the backend root, and listen 8080 collided with the backend's own port instead of serving on 80.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the trailing slash is cosmetic and listen 8080 was the proxy's port. Wrong because the slash changes URI rewriting and the proxy should listen on 80. Avoidable by matching the location and proxy_pass slash conventions and setting listen 80.
impact: All /api/* requests returned 404 from the backend root, and the proxy was unreachable on the expected port until reconfigured.
correct_action: Use 'proxy_pass http://backend:8080;' (no trailing slash) under 'location /api/' and 'listen 80;'.
recovery_plan: Reproduce the 404 on /api/users
Inspect the location/proxy_pass slash and listen directives
Remove the trailing slash and fix listen to 80
Run nginx -t and reload
Verify /api/* routes resolve correctly
evaluation_criteria: Checks the proxy_pass trailing-slash matches the intended URI handling
Detects an incorrect listen port
Verifies prefixed paths reach the correct upstream path

task: Add an upstream health check to Kong
user_request: Mark the backend unhealthy after 3 failed checks.
agent_action: Agent called the Kong upstreams API setting healthchecks.active.unhealthy.http_failures to 3 but put it under 'healthy' instead of 'unhealthy', and set the interval in minutes (1) where seconds were expected.
failure_type: Misplaced threshold under wrong key and wrong time unit
root_cause: The failure threshold landed in the healthy block (which expects successes) and an interval of 1 was interpreted as 1 second, probing far more aggressively than intended.
why_it_failed: Assumption: nested keys are interchangeable and interval is in minutes. Wrong because healthy/unhealthy blocks have distinct semantics and intervals are seconds. Avoidable by reading the upstream healthcheck schema and placing http_failures under 'unhealthy' with interval 60.
impact: Backends were never marked unhealthy on failures, so dead nodes kept receiving traffic.
correct_action: Set healthchecks.active.unhealthy.http_failures=3 and a sensible interval in seconds.
recovery_plan: Notice dead nodes still serving traffic
Read the upstream healthcheck config
Move http_failures under the unhealthy block
Set interval to the intended seconds value
Verify nodes flip to unhealthy after 3 failures
evaluation_criteria: Checks the failure threshold is under the unhealthy block
Detects a wrong time-unit for interval
Verifies unhealthy detection triggers as configured

task: Route a subset of traffic with an nginx map
user_request: Send 10% of /checkout traffic to the canary upstream.
agent_action: Agent configured split_clients with the percentage written as '10' instead of '10%', and referenced variable $request_id whose distribution is not uniform for weighting.
failure_type: Wrong percentage literal format in split_clients
root_cause: split_clients requires a percentage suffix ('10%'); the bare '10' failed to parse the weight, so the canary bucket got either 0% or a config error on reload.
why_it_failed: Assumption: split_clients takes a bare number. Wrong because it needs an explicit '%' and a uniformly-distributed key like $remote_addr or a hashed cookie. Avoidable by writing '10% canary;' and choosing a uniform hash key.
impact: The canary received no traffic (or the reload failed), so the new checkout build got zero real validation before full rollout.
correct_action: Use 'split_clients "${remote_addr}" $variant { 10% canary; * stable; }'.
recovery_plan: Notice canary receives ~0 traffic
Run nginx -t to surface the parse issue
Rewrite the weight as '10%' and use a uniform key
Reload nginx
Verify ~10% of requests hit the canary
evaluation_criteria: Checks the split weight includes the percent suffix
Detects a non-uniform hash key for weighting
Verifies the canary receives the intended share

task: Aggregate monthly revenue from the warehouse
user_request: Give me total revenue by month for 2025.
agent_action: Agent ran a BigQuery query summing 'amount' but filtered WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31', and grouped by EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) without the year, on a timestamp column stored in UTC while the business reports in US/Eastern.
failure_type: Off-by-one date range and ungrouped year plus timezone mismatch
root_cause: BETWEEN excluded the last day's late-UTC orders and the UTC-vs-Eastern shift moved boundary-day orders into the wrong month; grouping by month alone would also collide years in a multi-year table.
why_it_failed: Assumption: BETWEEN on a date literal covers the full year and UTC equals local. Wrong because timestamps past midnight Eastern fall on the next UTC day and Dec 31 23:59 ET was excluded. Avoidable by using order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND < '2026-01-01' on the timezone-converted column.
impact: December revenue was understated and a few orders landed in the wrong month, skewing the finance dashboard.
correct_action: Convert the timestamp to US/Eastern, filter with a half-open >= AND < range, and group by year and month.
recovery_plan: Notice December totals look low
Inspect the BETWEEN bounds and timezone handling
Rewrite with DATETIME(ts,'US/Eastern') and a half-open range
Group by year and month
Reconcile totals against the ledger
evaluation_criteria: Checks the date range is half-open and inclusive of the final day
Detects a UTC/local timezone mismatch on a timestamp
Verifies grouping disambiguates year

task: Backfill a Snowflake table for one partition
user_request: Reload sales data for 2025-03 only.
agent_action: Agent ran a Snowflake DELETE then INSERT but the DELETE used WHERE month = 3 instead of WHERE order_month = '2025-03', deleting March across all years.
failure_type: Wrong predicate column/value scoping the delete
root_cause: The predicate matched any row where a 'month' field equaled 3 regardless of year, so March 2022, 2023, and 2024 rows were deleted alongside 2025.
why_it_failed: Assumption: filtering month=3 isolates March 2025. Wrong because the table holds multiple years and the predicate ignored year. Avoidable by scoping on the year+month partition key and previewing the row count with a SELECT first.
impact: Four years of March sales were deleted from production, requiring a Time Travel restore.
correct_action: Scope the DELETE with order_month = '2025-03' (or year=2025 AND month=3) after a SELECT COUNT preview.
recovery_plan: Detect the unexpectedly large deleted row count
Halt the pipeline
Restore the table via Snowflake Time Travel (AT/BEFORE)
Re-run the delete with the year-scoped predicate
Re-insert only the 2025-03 partition and reconcile counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the delete predicate scopes to the exact year+month
Detects a year-agnostic predicate on a multi-year table
Verifies a count preview preceded the destructive write

task: Join orders to customers in a warehouse report
user_request: Show order totals with each customer's name.
agent_action: Agent wrote a BigQuery JOIN ON o.customer_id = c.id but customer_id in orders is a string-formatted external id while c.id is an INT64 surrogate key, so it CAST c.id to string and matched on the wrong column.
failure_type: Joining on the wrong key column with a type cast papering over it
root_cause: orders.customer_id holds the external CRM id, not the warehouse surrogate c.id; the cast made the types match but the values never aligned, producing a near-empty inner join.
why_it_failed: Assumption: customer_id maps to c.id. Wrong because customer_id maps to c.external_ref. Avoidable by inspecting the schema/lineage and joining o.customer_id = c.external_ref.
impact: The report showed almost no rows (silent inner-join drop), and a stakeholder nearly concluded order volume had collapsed.
correct_action: Join orders.customer_id = customers.external_ref with matching types, no spurious cast.
recovery_plan: Notice the result set is suspiciously small
Inspect both tables' schemas and key semantics
Rewrite the join on the correct external_ref key
Re-run and compare row counts to orders total
Validate a sample of joined names
evaluation_criteria: Checks the join uses semantically matching keys
Detects a cast masking a wrong-column join
Verifies joined row count matches expectations

task: Export a filtered dataset to GCS
user_request: Export Q4 2025 orders to a CSV in our exports bucket.
agent_action: Agent ran bigquery EXPORT DATA with uri 'gs://exports/orders/*.csv' but set format 'JSON' in the OPTIONS while naming files .csv, and filtered quarter='Q4' on a column that stores quarter as integer 4.
failure_type: Mismatched format option and wrong-typed filter literal
root_cause: format='JSON' wrote JSON content into .csv-named files, and the predicate quarter='Q4' matched zero rows because the column is an INT64 holding 4.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the extension sets the format and quarter is a string 'Q4'. Wrong because EXPORT honors the format OPTION not the filename, and the column type is integer. Avoidable by setting format='CSV' and filtering quarter=4.
impact: Downstream consumers got empty, mislabeled files and a loader broke on unexpected JSON.
correct_action: Set format='CSV', keep .csv uris, and filter quarter=4 (integer).
recovery_plan: See empty/mislabeled export files and loader errors
Check the EXPORT OPTIONS format and the quarter predicate type
Set format to CSV and fix the filter to quarter=4
Re-run the export
Verify file content and row counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the format OPTION matches the file extension
Detects a string literal filtered against an integer column
Verifies exported files are non-empty and correctly formatted

task: Grant a calendar's free/busy access to a service account
user_request: Let the scheduling bot read free/busy on the team calendar.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__google_calendar__acl_insert with role 'writer' and scope.type 'user' but scope.value set to the calendarId instead of the service account's email.
failure_type: Over-broad role enum and wrong scope.value identifier
root_cause: role 'writer' grants edit rights (the user asked only for free/busy reads), and scope.value being a calendarId rather than the service-account email meant the ACL targeted the wrong principal.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'writer' is the read role and any id fits scope.value. Wrong because free/busy maps to role 'freeBusyReader' and scope.value must be the principal's email. Avoidable by selecting role 'freeBusyReader' and passing the service account's email.
impact: A bot was nearly granted full write access to the team calendar, a privilege-escalation risk, and the ACL pointed at the wrong entity.
correct_action: Insert an ACL with role 'freeBusyReader' and scope {type:'user', value:'<service-account>@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com'}.
recovery_plan: Audit the new ACL entry on the calendar
Delete the over-privileged writer rule
Insert a freeBusyReader rule scoped to the service account email
Verify the bot can read free/busy but not edit
Review other ACLs for similar over-grants
evaluation_criteria: Checks the ACL role matches the least-privilege intent
Detects scope.value pointing at the wrong principal type
Verifies the grant is read-only free/busy

task: Archive completed tasks in a Notion database
user_request: Archive all tasks marked Done.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__notion__pages_update on matched pages setting 'in_trash' to true (deleting them) instead of setting 'archived' to true, and filtered Status equals 'done' (lowercase) missing the 'Done' option.
failure_type: Wrong boolean field (trash vs archive) and case-mismatched filter
root_cause: in_trash=true moves pages to trash for permanent deletion rather than archiving, and the lowercase 'done' filter matched fewer pages than intended, so the wrong set was destructively trashed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: in_trash and archived are equivalent and select names are case-insensitive. Wrong because in_trash deletes and Notion options are exact-case. Avoidable by setting archived=true and filtering the exact option 'Done'.
impact: A subset of completed tasks was sent to trash (recoverable for 30 days but alarming), while some Done tasks were skipped entirely.
correct_action: Filter Status equals exactly 'Done' and set archived=true on each matched page.
recovery_plan: Notice pages in trash rather than archived and some Done tasks untouched
Restore the trashed pages
Re-query with the exact 'Done' option name
Set archived=true on the full matched set
Verify the active view excludes archived Done tasks
evaluation_criteria: Checks archived (not in_trash) was used for archiving
Detects a case-mismatched select filter
Verifies all and only Done tasks were archived
